newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares rally at noon on MFN move.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares rally at noon on MFN move.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Tuesday morning sharply higher on a rebound after U.S. President Bill Clinton said he planned to renew China's most favoured nation (MFN) trade status, traders said.
The foreign currency B index ended the morning at 170.97 points, up 4.11 points or 2.47 percent on turnover of HK$43.2 million.
"The B index was poised for a technical rebound anyway, and Clinton's announcement pushed it higher," a trader at J&A Securities said.
President Clinton announced in Washington on Monday he would renew China's MFN trade privileges for another year, though the decision will face opposition in the U.S. Congress.
The B share index on Monday began a rally after falling 7.80 percent on Friday due to the suspension of two local currency A share companies.
"But the index is likely to ease in the afternoon as the turnover is tiny," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
The domestic currency A index gained 8.42 points or 1.78 percent to 480.86 on turnover of 4.0 billion yuan.
"Investors in the A share market were cheered by Shenzhen Development Bank's performance despite an investigation into irregularities," the J&A analyst said.

Shenzhen Development Bank Co, which was suspended for Monday morning trading after announcing it might have been involved in stock trading irregularities, added 1.90 yuan or 5.1 percent to 38.87 yuan.
In the B share market, Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd was the top gainer, rising HK$0.22, or 5.05 percent, to HK$4.58.
